intro: Watch an experienced skater link a 360 flip into a backside 180 and it can look like magic. It is not. Every advanced trick is built from simpler pieces: a pop, a scoop, a flick, a turn of the shoulders. In this unit you take apart frontside and backside 180s, the 360 flip, varial flips, rock to fakie, airs and grabs, and see how each one grows out of tricks you may already know.

You will also look at the physics that decides how a trick moves. A spin must start while your feet push on the ground, because in the air your angular momentum cannot change. A deck rolls around its length far more easily than it spins flat, which is why a kickflip needs only a flick. Worked examples show the arithmetic, from time in the air to the force of a fall.

The second chapter turns to learning itself. Research on motor learning explains why short, spaced sessions beat long ones, why mixing tricks helps, why sleep matters, and how video and one clear cue speed things up. You will build a fear ladder, practice falling small, and plan sessions you can repeat safely for months.
bigQuestion: How are advanced tricks built from simpler ones, and what does science say about the fastest, safest way to learn them?

timeline.t: Hermann Ebbinghaus publishes memory experiments showing the value of spaced repetition
Paul Fitts and Michael Posner describe three stages of learning a motor skill
Pool and park skaters begin flying above the coping; Alan Gelfand's ollie on transition
Shea and Morgan publish a study showing that mixed practice improves later performance
Thrasher magazine is founded, printing photo sequences of tricks
Rodney Mullen develops many flat-ground tricks, including the impossible
The Bones Brigade Video Show lets skaters study tricks on VHS
Tony Hawk lands the 900, two and a half turns, at the X Games in San Francisco
The Tony Hawk Foundation is started to help build public skateparks
Oliver Percovich founds Skateistan in Kabul, Afghanistan

rolling backward in your normal stance

the metal pipe or hard edge along the top of a ramp or pool

test.q: In a backside 180 ollie, what faces the direction of travel first?
test.why: In a backside turn, the back leads.

test.q: Why does tucking in during a spin make a skater spin faster?
choices: A smaller I means a bigger ω, since L = Iω stays the same.
test.why: Angular momentum stays the same, so lowering I raises the spin rate.

test.q: Which two tricks make a 360 flip?
test.why: The 360 flip combines a backside 360 shove-it and a kickflip.

test.q: Which trick is a backside pop shove-it plus a kickflip?
test.why: A varial kickflip combines a backside pop shove-it with a kickflip.

test.q: In the plank model, why is a flat spin about 17 times harder to start than a flip?
choices: The mass sits much farther from the vertical axis than from the long axis.
test.why: Mass far from the axis raises the moment of inertia; (0.64 + 0.04) ÷ 0.04 = 17.

test.q: During a rock to fakie, where is the coping?
choices: under the middle of the board, between the trucks
test.why: In the rock, the board rests on the coping between the trucks.

test.q: An air rises 0.50 m above the coping. About how long is it in the air?
Which grab is the back hand on the toe-side edge between the feet?
test.why: An indy is the back hand on the toe-side edge between the feet.

test.q: Which stage of learning comes after the cognitive stage?
test.why: Fitts and Posner's stages go cognitive, associative, autonomous.

test.q: Why might a skater land a trick on Monday after missing it all Friday?
choices: Rest and sleep let the skill consolidate, and fatigue was gone.
Fear is stronger after a weekend.
test.why: Consolidation during rest and sleep, plus fresh legs, can improve a skill without extra practice.

choices: the same trick in the same spot 100 times
changing speed, place or trick order during practice
test.why: Variable practice changes the conditions of practice.

test.q: A pop lasts 15 frames on a 30-frames-per-second video. About how high was it? (h = g·t²/8)
A 60 kg skater at 3 m/s stops in 0.05 s. What is the average force?
During a knee slide, what should the skater do?
choices: reach for the ramp with straight arms
sit back toward the heels with hands near the chest
test.why: Sitting back with hands up keeps the slide smooth and the arms safe.

choices: a list of small steps from least to most scary
test.why: A fear ladder breaks a scary trick into small steps practiced one at a time.

write.prompt: Choose one advanced trick from this unit, such as the 360 flip, a backside 180 or rock to fakie. Explain its steps in order, with what the front foot and back foot do. Name the simpler tricks it builds on and the physics behind it. Then describe a one-week practice plan for it using at least two ideas from the science of practice.
tips: Use front foot and back foot, not left and right.
Name the axis or the force involved, and show one calculation if it fits.
List the tricks that come before yours in its progression.
Include spacing, variety, one cue, rest or a fear ladder in your plan.
Put safety gear in the plan naturally, not as a list at the end.
